headline: High-risk shared filesystem and shell privileges make Cursor↔MinerU prone to prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor can read/write workspace files, clipboard, and use MCP; MinerU can ingest local documents and expose an MCP server. That creates a plausible content bridge where MinerU outputs or parsed documents can be copied into Cursor and treated as instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so interaction risk is real but not clearly automatic.
conditions: IF MinerU output is pasted or saved into a Cursor-opened file without provenance labels, injection is possible.
IF either agent is configured to auto-ingest shared MCP content, attacker-controlled text can steer tool use.
mitigations: Disable copy/paste of raw model output into active prompts.
Use separate folders for MinerU outputs and Cursor workspaces.
Add a provenance header to all imported documents.
Turn off MCP endpoints not needed for the task.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping at the handoff boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches source code, open files, clipboard contents, and broad network egress; MinerU processes PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, and OCR text. If they share a local filesystem, sensitive documents extracted by MinerU can be opened by Cursor and then sent to third-party model providers. The leakage path is plausible in default workflows, though not proven automatic.
conditions: IF MinerU writes extracted text into a workspace Cursor can read, Cursor may transmit that content to external model providers.
IF the same local directory holds sensitive documents and code, cross-exposure can occur.
mitigations: Keep MinerU outputs in a separate directory.
Avoid opening sensitive extracts in Cursor unless necessary.
Disable or restrict network egress for Cursor on sensitive projects.
Use redacted sample documents for extraction tests.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level access controls between the tools.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cursor has unrestricted filesystem write, shell execution, and git-state modification; MinerU is concurrent and exposes file/API/MCP interfaces. If both operate on the same workspace, Cursor can overwrite or commit files while MinerU reads or processes them, creating race conditions and corrupted outputs. Uncertainty about locking pushes this to high rather than medium.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory, concurrent writes or reads can race.
IF Cursor runs in Yolo mode, it can modify files while MinerU is still processing them.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Pause one agent before the other writes to shared files.
Avoid git commits until MinerU finishes processing.
Use file snapshots before handoff.
requires-engineering: add locking or transactional workspace coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor can act on generated code and modify git state, while MinerU produces extracted text, tables, and OCR output. If Cursor treats MinerU output as authoritative without verification, extraction errors can cascade into incorrect code, docs, or commits. The pair has a clear handoff path, but no evidence that this is fully automated by default.
conditions: IF Cursor uses MinerU extraction as ground truth without human review, downstream edits can propagate errors.
IF extracted tables or OCR text are copied into prompts, hallucinated structure can be amplified.
mitigations: Require human review of extracted facts before editing.
Compare MinerU output against the source document for critical fields.
Use a checklist for any commit based on extracted data.
Limit automation to non-destructive drafts.
requires-engineering: add verification gates between extraction and action-taking.

E_compliance.rationale: MinerU is documented as private and fully offline, while Cursor uses broad network egress and third-party model providers. For regulated or residency-sensitive data, the mismatch can create compliance exposure if the same documents are processed in Cursor after extraction. This is a policy mismatch rather than a guaranteed breach, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated documents extracted by MinerU are then sent through Cursor prompts, residency or retention obligations may be violated.
IF the deployment requires offline-only processing, Cursor's network egress conflicts with that requirement.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Cursor prompts.
Use MinerU only for offline extraction on sensitive files.
Review vendor retention settings before upload.
Separate compliant and non-compliant workflows.
requires-engineering: route regulated workloads to an offline-only stack.
